newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HOME REFINANCING SEEN RISING BEFORE SMALL DIP.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HOME REFINANCING SEEN RISING BEFORE SMALL DIP.

text.p: Refinancing activity represented more than one-third of all mortgage applications in the latest reporting week, and won't soon drop significantly, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association of America (MBA).

The rate spike last Friday will take some of the steam out of mortgage refinancings, said David Lereah, MBA chief economist. Rates remain low enough, however, to keep refinancings running around 30 percent of all applications, up sharply from a more typical 20 percent level, he said.
The MBA's refinancing index gained 15.7 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis to 689.3 in the week ended August 7.
Lereah predicted the index would pierce 700 in next Thursday's report before settling down to the 500 level.

That would still represent "real good, healthy applications activity," he said. Refinancings are "completely interest-rate sensitive," he added, predicting that interest rates would remain in their current range for the near term.

An increase in the seasonally adjusted home purchase index further indicated that housing demand remained buoyant. The 2.8 percent advance to 211.7 suggested growth was not limited to a usual summer increase in homebuying, according to Lereah.

The home purchase applications measure is a leading indicator of home sales. September home sales, as a result, "will still be relatively strong," the MBA chief economist said. "We still have a very healthy housing market."

During the latest reporting period, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.52 percent, up marginally from 7.51 percent the prior week. Points increased on average to 1.19 from 1.14, including the origination fee, for 80 percent loan-to-value mortgages.

"We'll continue to have a positive rate environment in the near term," said Lereah. "Markets are no longer anxious about the Fed raising rates at the next (policy-setting) meeting, which sould keep refinancings at a very healthy clip.
The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee next meets on August 19.
